# Part 1 — What is Quarto? {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Quarto at a Glance

- Quarto is an **open-source scientific publishing system** built on Pandoc
- Successor to R Markdown — works with R, Python, Julia, and Observable JS
- One `.qmd` file → HTML, PDF, Word, slides, dashboards, books, websites
- Separates **content** (text + code) from **presentation** (YAML options)

```
my_report.qmd  →  Render  →  my_report.html
                          →  my_report.pdf
                          →  my_report.docx
```

---

## Installing Quarto

1. Download from [quarto.org](https://quarto.org)
2. Quarto comes pre-installed with **RStudio 2022.07+**
3. Verify in terminal:

```bash
quarto --version
```

Required R packages:

```{r eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("knitr", "rmarkdown", "tidyverse"))
```

---

## The Anatomy of a .qmd File

Every Quarto file has three parts:

```
---
title: "My Report"       ← YAML front matter (metadata + options)
author: "Name"
format: html
---

Some **bold** text.      ← Markdown prose

`​`​`{r}               ← Code chunk
summary(cars)
`​`​`
```

---

# Part 2 — YAML Front Matter {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Basic YAML Options

```yaml
---
title: "Study Report"
subtitle: "Baseline Analysis"
author: "Dr. Researcher"
date: today
format: html
---
```

> `date: today` automatically inserts today's date at render time.

---

## Output Formats

```yaml
---
format: html          # Web page
format: pdf           # PDF (requires LaTeX or TinyTeX)
format: docx          # Microsoft Word
format: revealjs      # Slide deck
format: pptx          # PowerPoint
---
```

Install TinyTeX for PDF:

```{r eval=FALSE}
install.packages("tinytex")
tinytex::install_tinytex()
```

---

## HTML Format Options

```yaml
---
format:
  html:
    toc: true               # Table of contents
    toc-depth: 3            # Heading levels in TOC
    number-sections: true   # Numbered headings
    theme: flatly           # Bootstrap theme
    embed-resources: true   # Single self-contained file
    code-fold: true         # Collapsible code blocks
    code-tools: true        # Copy button + source button
---
```

---

## HTML Themes

Available Bootstrap themes:

`default`, `cerulean`, `cosmo`, `cyborg`, `darkly`, `flatly`, `journal`,  
`litera`, `lumen`, `lux`, `materia`, `minty`, `morph`, `pulse`, `quartz`,  
`sandstone`, `simplex`, `sketchy`, `slate`, `solar`, `spacelab`, `superhero`,  
`united`, `vapor`, `yeti`, `zephyr`

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme: flatly
```

---

## Word Format Options

```yaml
---
format:
  docx:
    reference-doc: my_template.docx   # Use a custom Word template
    toc: true
    number-sections: true
---
```

> Create a Word template by opening a blank `.docx` and modifying heading/body styles — save and reference it here.

---

## revealjs Slide Options

```yaml
---
format:
  revealjs:
    theme: simple          # simple, moon, night, sky, serif, solarized
    slide-number: true
    incremental: true      # Bullets appear one at a time
    embed-resources: true
    transition: slide      # none, fade, slide, convex, zoom
    chalkboard: true       # Enable drawing on slides
---
```

---

## Global Execute Options in YAML

```yaml
---
execute:
  echo: true        # Show code
  eval: true        # Run code
  warning: false    # Hide warnings
  message: false    # Hide messages
  error: false      # Hide errors (or true to continue on error)
  cache: true       # Cache chunk results
---
```

---

# Part 3 — Markdown Basics {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Text Formatting

```markdown
**bold**        *italic*        ***bold italic***

`inline code`   ~~strikethrough~~   ^superscript^   ~subscript~

> This is a blockquote

[Link text](https://quarto.org)

![Caption](image.png){width=60%}
```

---

## Headings

```markdown
# Level 1 Heading
## Level 2 Heading
### Level 3 Heading
#### Level 4 Heading
```

> In a revealjs deck, `##` creates a new slide. In HTML, it creates a section heading.

---

## Lists

```markdown
# Unordered
- Item one
- Item two
  - Nested item

# Ordered
1. First
2. Second
3. Third

# Task list
- [x] Done
- [ ] To do
```

---

## Tables in Markdown

```markdown
| Variable  | Type        | Example       |
|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| Age       | Continuous  | 34 years      |
| Sex       | Categorical | Male / Female |
| BMI       | Continuous  | 27.4          |
```

> Use the RStudio **Visual Editor** (Ctrl+Shift+F4) to insert and edit Markdown tables with a GUI.

---

## Callout Blocks

```markdown
::: {.callout-note}
This is a note.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
Pay attention to this.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
A helpful tip.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
This is important.
:::
```

---

## Divs and Spans for Custom Layout

```markdown
:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
Left column content
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
Right column content
:::

::::
```

---

# Part 4 — Code Chunks {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Anatomy of a Code Chunk

````markdown
```{r}
#| label: my-chunk
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
#| warning: false

summary(cars)
```
````

> `#|` is the **YAML-style chunk option** syntax — preferred in Quarto over the old `{r echo=TRUE}` inline format.

---

## Key Chunk Options

| Option | Values | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `echo` | true/false | Show code |
| `eval` | true/false | Run code |
| `output` | true/false/asis | Show output |
| `warning` | true/false | Show warnings |
| `message` | true/false | Show messages |
| `include` | true/false | Include chunk at all |
| `label` | string | Chunk name (for caching/cross-ref) |
| `fig-width` | number | Figure width in inches |
| `fig-height` | number | Figure height in inches |
| `fig-cap` | string | Figure caption |

---

## echo: false — Hide Code, Show Output

````markdown
```{r}
#| echo: false
summary(cars)
```
````

---

## eval: false — Show Code, Don't Run

````markdown
```{r}
#| eval: false
install.packages("gtsummary")
```
````

---

## include: false — Run Silently

````markdown
```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
p <- read_csv("data.csv")
```
````

> Code runs and results are available globally, but nothing is shown in the output.

---

## output: asis — Raw Output

````markdown
```{r}
#| output: asis
cat("**This text is bold in output.**")
```
````

---

## fig-cap and fig-alt

````markdown
```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of participant age"
#| fig-alt: "Histogram showing right-skewed distribution"
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4

hist(rnorm(100), main = "", xlab = "Age")
```
````

---

## Caching — Speed Up Long Renders

````markdown
```{r}
#| cache: true
#| label: slow-model

model <- lm(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars)
summary(model)
```
````

> Cache is invalidated automatically when the chunk code changes. Delete `*_cache/` folder to force re-run.

---

## Inline Code

Use backtick-r to embed computed values directly in prose:

```markdown
The mean age was `r round(mean(trial$age, na.rm = TRUE), 1)` years.
```

Renders as:

> The mean age was **47.2** years.

This makes results **fully reproducible** — update the data and the number updates automatically.

---

# Part 5 — Cross-References {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Figures

````markdown
```{r}
#| label: fig-age-hist
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of age"

hist(rnorm(100))
```

See @fig-age-hist for the distribution.
````

> Labels for figures must start with `fig-`.

---

## Tables

````markdown
```{r}
#| label: tbl-baseline
#| tbl-cap: "Baseline characteristics"

knitr::kable(head(mtcars))
```

See @tbl-baseline for baseline data.
````

> Labels for tables must start with `tbl-`.

---

## Sections

```markdown
## Methods {#sec-methods}

Details here.

As described in @sec-methods...
```

---

## Equations

Inline: `$E = mc^2$` → \(E = mc^2\)

Block:
```markdown
$$
\bar{x} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i
$$
```

# Part 6 — Output Customisation {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Table Output — knitr::kable()

```{r}
library(knitr)
kable(head(mtcars[, 1:5]), caption = "Table: First rows of mtcars")
```

---

## Table Output — kableExtra

```{r}
library(kableExtra)

kable(head(mtcars[, 1:4]), caption = "Styled table") |>
  kable_styling(
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
    full_width = FALSE
  ) |>
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE) |>
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C3E50", color = "white")
```

---

## Figure Layout — side by side

````markdown
```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "Left: Histogram"
#|   - "Right: Boxplot"

hist(rnorm(100))
boxplot(rnorm(100))
```
````

---

## Figure Layout — custom grid

````markdown
```{r}
#| layout: [[1,1], [1]]
hist(rnorm(100))
boxplot(rnorm(100))
plot(cars)
```
````

> `[[1,1], [1]]` means: row 1 has 2 equal-width plots; row 2 has 1 full-width plot.

---

## Page Breaks (Word/PDF)

```markdown
::: {.content-visible when-format="docx"}
\newpage
:::
```

Or universally:

```markdown
{{< pagebreak >}}
```

---

# Part 7 — Parameters {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Parameterised Reports

Define parameters in YAML and reference them in the document — render the same report for different groups or time periods.

```yaml
---
title: "District Report"
params:
  district: "Bareilly"
  year: 2026
---
```

Reference in code:

```{r eval=FALSE}
params$district   # "Bareilly"
params$year       # 2026

data_filtered <- data |> filter(district == params$district)
```

---

## Rendering with Different Parameters

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Render for each district
quarto::quarto_render(
  "district_report.qmd",
  execute_params = list(district = "Lucknow", year = 2026),
  output_file    = "lucknow_report.html"
)

quarto::quarto_render(
  "district_report.qmd",
  execute_params = list(district = "Agra", year = 2026),
  output_file    = "agra_report.html"
)
```

> This is powerful for generating **one report per site, district, or time period** automatically.

---

# Part 8 — Quarto Projects {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## What is a Quarto Project?

A project is a folder with a `_quarto.yml` configuration file that coordinates multiple `.qmd` files.

```
my_project/
├── _quarto.yml       ← project config
├── index.qmd         ← home / landing page
├── methods.qmd
├── results.qmd
├── references.bib
└── data/
```

---

## _quarto.yml — Website Project

```yaml
project:
  type: website

website:
  title: "My Research Site"
  navbar:
    left:
      - href: index.qmd
        text: Home
      - href: results.qmd
        text: Results
```

---

## _quarto.yml — Book Project

```yaml
project:
  type: book

book:
  title: "Field Epidemiology Manual"
  author: "Workshop Team"
  chapters:
    - index.qmd
    - intro.qmd
    - methods.qmd
    - results.qmd
    - references.qmd
```

---

## _quarto.yml — Shared Execute Options

```yaml
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
```

> Any execute option in `_quarto.yml` applies to **all files** in the project.

---

## Rendering a Project

```bash
# Render all files
quarto render

# Preview in browser with live reload
quarto preview

# Render one specific file
quarto render results.qmd
```

---

# Part 9 — Advanced Features {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Conditional Content by Format

```markdown
::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
This only appears in HTML output.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="docx"}
This only appears in Word output.
:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="pdf"}
This is hidden in PDF only.
:::
```

---

## Tabsets — Organise Content in Tabs

```markdown
::: {.panel-tabset}

## Table

```{r}
knitr::kable(head(mtcars))
```

## Plot

```{r}
plot(cars)
```

:::
```

> Tabsets work in HTML only. They collapse to sequential sections in Word/PDF.

---

## Code Folding and Annotation

```yaml
format:
  html:
    code-fold: true
    code-summary: "Show code"
```

Code annotation with `<1>` markers:

````markdown
```{r}
model <- lm(mpg ~ hp + wt, data = mtcars)  # <1>
summary(model)                              # <2>
```
1. Fit linear model with horsepower and weight as predictors.
2. Display model summary with coefficients and fit statistics.
````

---

## Bibliography and Citations

In YAML:

```yaml
bibliography: references.bib
csl: apa.csl     # Citation Style Language — APA, Vancouver, etc.
```

In text:

```markdown
As shown in previous studies [@smith2020; @jones2021],
the prevalence was high.
```

Renders as:

> As shown in previous studies (Smith, 2020; Jones, 2021), the prevalence was high.

---

## Shortcodes

```markdown
{{< var title >}}       ← Insert a YAML variable
{{< include file.qmd >}} ← Include another file
{{< pagebreak >}}       ← Insert a page break
{{< kbd Ctrl+Enter >}}  ← Render a keyboard shortcut
```

---

## Freeze — Large Projects

```yaml
execute:
  freeze: auto    # Re-run only if source changes
```

Or per-chunk:

````markdown
```{r}
#| freeze: true
expensive_computation()
```
````

> `freeze: auto` stores rendered outputs in `_freeze/` — prevents re-running unchanged chunks on every build.

---

## Lua Filters and Extensions

Add community extensions directly in the terminal:

```bash
# Add an extension
quarto add quarto-ext/fontawesome
quarto add quarto-journals/jama        # JAMA journal template
quarto add quarto-journals/plos        # PLOS template
```

Use in document:

```markdown
{{< fa user >}}    ← FontAwesome icon
```

---

## Publishing Quarto Documents

```bash
# Publish to Quarto Pub (free, public)
quarto publish quarto-pub

# Publish to GitHub Pages
quarto publish gh-pages

# Publish to Posit Connect (organisational)
quarto publish connect
```

---

## Quick Reference — Quarto Cheat Sheet

| Task | YAML / Syntax |
|---|---|
| HTML output | `format: html` |
| Word output | `format: docx` |
| Slides | `format: revealjs` |
| TOC | `toc: true` |
| Hide code | `echo: false` |
| Don't run | `eval: false` |
| Run silently | `include: false` |
| Figure caption | `#\| fig-cap: "..."` |
| Table caption | `#\| tbl-cap: "..."` |
| Cross-ref figure | `@fig-label` |
| Inline code | `` `r expr` `` |
| Parameters | `params: key: value` |
| Conditional content | `when-format="html"` |
| Tabsets | `.panel-tabset` |
| Page break | `{{< pagebreak >}}` |
| Freeze | `freeze: auto` |
| Render project | `quarto render` |
| Preview | `quarto preview` |
